relevance_note: A single-centre lysosomal storage disease cohort that includes one Danon disease patient with individual-level detail: "The patient with DD had massive left ventricular hypertrophy" and "The patient with DD was diagnosed with a WPW syndrome."
method_note: Written by hand from my reading, assembled with a short Python script; no table was transcribed by script. Scope: of 39 LSD patients only the one Danon disease (DD) patient is in scope; the other 38 (MPS, AFD, Pompe, ML) get no rows. Label: a cohort paper, not a case report, and the paper uses no own label ('the patient with DD' is a role phrase), so rule 6 gives 'unnamed person 1'; the label span quotes the first mention ('DD (1)' in the abstract). No variants row: the paper prints no LAMP2 variant and does not state that this patient had genetic testing (inclusion required 'a biochemical or genetic diagnosis', without saying which applied to whom), so clinical_diagnosis_basis is 'not reported' and no variant is tied to the person. Sex not stated for the DD patient (the Discussion's 'male teenager' is general advice, not about this patient). Age 15 is the age at the most recent echocardiogram (Table 2) and in the Fig. 1 legend; recorded as age at last evaluation. The patient died during follow-up; age at death and cause not stated individually (only cohort-level: respiratory failure in 7, septicemia in 1; 'no patient died due to a cardiac cause' in the abstract), so cause_of_death is 'not reported'. Group-level counts in Tables 3-7 for the oLSD group (n = 6/5) were not assigned to the DD patient (e.g. Table 6 Preexcitation oLSD '1 (20%)', AF '1/2 (50%)', NYHA III 'One patient of the oLSD group') because they do not name the patient; WPW comes from the text sentence. Exclusions from cohort-wide named statements ('None of our patients with any LSD had a left ventricular outflow tract gradient'; 'There were no patients with ventricular tachycardias'; 'no higher degree AV blockage was found in our patient cohort') are marked 'inferred from group statement'. Absence of VT does not exclude the composite checklist item 'ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation'; 'no higher degree AV block' (and the single 2nd-degree block in an MPS patient) does not address first-degree block, so the checklist 'atrioventricular block' stays not reported. CONTRADICTION: Results say 'Significant pulmonary hypertension was only seen in MPS (2/9, 22%)' and Table 4 gives PHT 0/5 in oLSD, but the next sentence says no AFD or oLSD patient had significantly elevated pulmonary artery pressures 'except for the patient with DD'. Both rows emitted (observed and excluded); pulmonary hypertension is not a checklist item. The Discussion statement on 'the patients with Danon disease who died during follow-up' is plural although only one DD patient is in the cohort; read as this patient. Reference [24] (Balmer et al., with an author of this paper) is cited for Danon disease in Table 1, but the paper does not say its patient was described there, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null. Fig. 1 legend ('15-Year old patient with Danon disease') used for the 39 mm wall measurement and ECG LVH signs.
